title: Stitch: why does the peacock shake like that?

scenes.headline: He's train-rattling
scenes.body: High-speed video shows peacocks vibrating their feathers about 25 times a second.

scenes.headline: It makes a pulsing buzz, too
scenes.body: Peacocks were filmed rattling for over 25 minutes.

caption:
Answering the question everyone asks under peacock videos.

The display is aimed at peahens, and males with longer trains used slightly higher vibration frequencies on average.

Source: Dakin et al. 2016, PLOS ONE.  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Stitch demo: in real use the first beat is the other creator's reel via Instagram's native Stitch (allowed); here a CC clip stands in. Our answer adds peer-reviewed data.
